days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Roque de los Muchachos
stops.detail: The depression that forms the Caldera is located between 600 and 900 meters above sea level, while the crest that forms the rocky fence surrounding it reaches 2,426 meters at its highest point, the so-called Roque de los Muchachos, where the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory is located.

stops.name: Taburiente
stops.detail: The two main hydrological basins are those of Taburiente and Almendro Amargo, which converge at the point where the Barranco de las Angustias begins, the only natural outlet of the Caldera, where it flows into the sea.

stops.name: Barranco de las Angustias
stops.detail: For these reasons, it can be seen at the beginning of the Barranco de las Angustias that the last two tributaries in the original walls of the caldera drain toward its center, which could not be explained by an explosive eruption.

stops.name: Salto de la Desfondada
stops.detail: As an example, the Salto de la Desfondada has a drop of about 150 m.

stops.name: Río de Almendro Amargo
stops.detail: In most sources we find clean and crystalline waters, but there are also others altered in their composition by a large amount of materials, such as those coming from the Río de Almendro Amargo, with a reddish-yellow color due to the iron materials in the area.
